title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. On the previous page Grothendieck has homomorphisms from M (and M^!) and from π_1^et(·_Q) into groups built from Ẑ^* and symmetric/profinite data: G_{ρ,σ} = Ẑ^*·S^{+∧} and N_σ^Gal = Ẑ^*·Ẑ (semi-direct). He asks whether they are surjective. One of them reduces to the cyclotomic condition. On this page he proposes to relate these homomorphisms to the tower of Fermat curves over Q.

Definitions (220).
- X_n ⊂ P^2_Q is the Fermat curve x_0^n + x_1^n + x_∞^n = 0, with coordinates indexed by the set {0,1,∞}.
- U_n ⊂ X_n is the open set where x_0 x_1 x_∞ ≠ 0.

Symmetries (221).
- The finite Q-group scheme F_n^0 = μ_n^{{0,1,∞}}/μ_n (diagonal) acts on X_n by scaling the coordinates. It is non-constant over Q, of order n^2.
- S_3 = S_{{0,1,∞}} acts on X_n by permuting the coordinates.
- Together they give the semi-direct product F_n = S_3 ⋉ F_n^0. For n ≥ 4 this is the full automorphism group of the Fermat curve.

Quotient (222). Grothendieck writes X_n/F_n^0 ≅ X_1 ≅ U_{0,3}, S_3-equivariantly. Here X_1 is the line x_0 + x_1 + x_∞ = 0 ≅ P^1, via (x_0,x_1,x_∞) ↦ (x_0^n, x_1^n, x_∞^n). Correctly: X_n → X_1 = P^1 is a Galois cover with group F_n^0, ramified only over the three coordinate points. Its restriction U_n → U_1 = P^1 − {0,1,∞} = U_{0,3} is an F_n^0-torsor.

Transition maps (223)–(224). For n = n'd, the map x_i ↦ x_i^d gives X_n → X_{n'}. It is a principal cover with group μ_d^3/μ_d over U_{n'} (as the next page corrects), not over all of X_{n'}. It is compatible with the epimorphism F_n → F_{n'}, which is the identity on S_3 and d-th power on μ_n^3/μ_n. The kernel is μ_d^3/μ_d (both have order d^2).

Limit (next page, 226). X_∞ = lim X_n, U_∞ = lim U_n, and F_∞ = S_3 ⋉ (Ẑ^{{0,1,∞}}/Ẑ) ⊗ T(G_m) = S_3 ⋉ Ẑ(1)^2. This is just the maximal abelian pro-cover of U_{0,3,Q̄}: F_∞^0 = π_1(U_{0,3,Q̄})^ab with its Galois (cyclotomic) twist, extended by the S_3 symmetries.

Purpose. To test the surjectivity and cyclotomic questions about M, M^! → Ẑ^*·(…) by realising the abelian (Ẑ(1)^2 ⋊ S_3) level of the anabelian/Teichmüller picture concretely through the Fermat tower. The margin indicates the notation and the role of F_∞ will be revisited at p. 719'.
errors: (222) is written X_n/F_n^0 ≅ X_1 ≅ U_{0,3}. But X_1 (the line x_0+x_1+x_∞=0) is ≅ P^1. The correct statements are X_n/F_n^0 ≅ X_1 ≅ P^1 and U_n/F_n^0 ≅ U_1 ≅ U_{0,3} = P^1 − {0,1,∞}.

The page says X_n becomes a principal cover (torsor) over X_{n'} with group μ_d^3/μ_d. This is only true over U_{n'}: the map is ramified over the points of X_{n'} where a coordinate vanishes. The next page corrects this to U_n → U_{n'}.
In the crossed-out/partial formula for F_n → F_{n'}, the S_3 component appears as g ↦ g^d. It should be g ↦ g, as the next page states.
Minor: the next page writes the kernel of F_n → F_{n'} as μ_d^{{0,1,∞}}. It should be μ_d^{{0,1,∞}}/μ_d (order d^2).

ideas.what: Fermat curves X_n as Galois covers of P^1 branched over {0,1,∞}, with group μ_n^3/μ_n, and automorphism group S_3 ⋉ μ_n^3/μ_n over Q
ideas.modern_name: Fermat curve as abelian cover of P^1 − {0,1,∞}; automorphism group of the Fermat curve
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Weil, Jacobi sums; Rohrlich 1977; automorphism group: Tzermias, Leopoldt and others)
ideas.where_published: not in Esquisse/Longue Marche as far as known; standard in literature

ideas.what: The Fermat tower (U_n) with transition maps x_i ↦ x_i^d and limit group F_∞ = S_3 ⋉ Ẑ(1)^2, i.e. the maximal abelian pro-cover of P^1 − {0,1,∞} with its S_3 and Galois symmetries
ideas.modern_name: Fermat tower / π_1^ab of P^1 − {0,1,∞}; Ihara's metabelian Galois representation via Fermat Jacobians
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara (Annals 1986, 'Profinite braid groups, Galois representations and complex multiplications'), Anderson (hyperadelic gamma function), Coleman, Deligne

ideas.what: Plan to relate the surjectivity and cyclotomic-condition questions for homomorphisms from M (and from π_1^et over Q) into Ẑ^*-semidirect groups to the Galois action on the Fermat tower
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on the abelian/metabelian quotient of π_1(P^1 − {0,1,∞}); the abelian level of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller programme

missed.claim: Historical: in the Longue Marche continuation (presumably c. 1981), Grothendieck sets up the Fermat tower, with its S_3 ⋉ Ẑ(1)^2 symmetry group, as the concrete abelian level of his π_1(U_{0,3})/Teichmüller analysis over Q. This predates Ihara's systematic use of the Fermat tower and Jacobi sums for the Galois action on π_1^{ab}/π_1^{metab} of P^1 − {0,1,∞}. The mathematics on this page is standard, so the novelty is priority/context only.
missed.quote: J'ai envie de mettre ces homomorphismes en relation avec la "tour" des courbes algébriques définies sur Q, indexées par n ∈ N^*
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that Grothendieck independently intended to link his anabelian/Teichmüller homomorphisms to Fermat curves (Ihara's later route). Whether pages up to 719' push to the metabelian level or Jacobi-sum formulas would be worth checking.

deep.surprise_reason: Standard Fermat-curve material; interest is only historical, as an early (pre-Ihara) intention to connect the anabelian programme to the Fermat tower.
transcription_corrections: In the S_3 part of the map F_n → F_{n'} (bottom right), the reading g ↦ g^d is uncertain/partly struck. The intended map is g ↦ g, as confirmed on the next page.

Margin note is only partly legible. It reads roughly 'Notation F_n pas très heureuse – il est possible qu'il y aura besoin plutôt de la suite ... F_∞ ... revêtements de Fermat ... U_∞ ... (voir p. 719')'. Treat the middle words as uncertain.
'(courbe de Fermat d'indice n)' is correct. In (220) a crossed-out character precedes x_1^n; the equation is x_0^n + x_1^n + x_∞^n = 0.
